problem: Prior zero-shot object navigation methods (CoW, ESC) either handle only object-category goals or pick frontiers with a single-pass LLM score or hand-crafted PSL rules, so they fail on language-described goals (spatial/appearance cues) and make sub-optimal frontier choices.
motivation: Real human-robot interaction needs goals given as natural language (e.g. 'alarm clock on a dresser near a desk lamp'), as in the PASTURE benchmark. Standard LLMs cannot self-assess their decisions, so frontier selection benefits from deliberate multi-path reasoning with backtracking.
key_idea: Use Tree-of-Thoughts prompting of an LLM (GPT-3.5) to select exploration frontiers from a GLIP-based semantic map, plus an LLM-based goal identification step that checks whether the reached object matches the full language description.
insight: Making the LLM reason with ToT (multi-expert deliberation) rather than directly picking a frontier improves the Pasture uncommon split from 29.8 to 36.9 SR (12.4 to 16.6 SWPL). Goal verification with an LLM on a VLM-generated scene description beats GLIP grounding (12.6 SR) and ViLT VQA (18.3 SR) on spatially described goals (21.7 SR), so language-level reasoning matters for complex instructions.
method: VLM Understanding: GLIP is prompted with object and room category prompts on the RGB image to give detected objects, rooms and bounding boxes.

Semantic Mapping: depth and pose are back-projected to 3D voxels and projected top-down into a 2D navigation map, then object and room semantics are overlaid to form a semantic map M_t; candidate frontiers come from ESC's pipeline.

ToT Reasoning and Exploration: frontiers are described as 'location #i, near <room>, where <objects> are also found'; the LLM, prompted with ten simulated experts (decomposition, step-wise generation with backtracking, likelihood evaluation, consensus search), returns the most likely frontier index with a likelihood.
Goal Identification: a VLM converts the current view to text, and GPT-3.5 compares it with the instruction's spatial/appearance description to confirm the target.
Frontier-based exploration: the agent navigates to the chosen frontier and repeats until a matching goal is verified.

setting.backbone: GLIP (frozen) + GPT-3.5 (frozen, ToT prompting and goal identification); ViLT/VLM for captioning
setting.action_space: frontier-based exploration with low-level navigation to selected map frontiers

numbers.extra: training-free; Avg over 7 PASTURE splits; per-split SR: Unc. 36.9, App. 35.0, Space 33.3, App. dist. 21.9, Space dist. 21.7, Hid. 22.8, Hid. dist. 26.4

numbers_note: PASTURE is not in the canonical list, so it is labelled other:PASTURE; metric is SWPL (as printed) rather than SPL. Ablation numbers (Tables 2-3) are on splits and not listed as separate entries.
results: VLTNet gets 28.2 SR / 14.0 SWPL average on PASTURE, beating OWL (21.1 SR / 12.6 SWPL) and ESC on the uncommon split (36.9 vs 35.5), with large gains on appearance (35.0 vs 26.9) and spatial (33.3 vs 19.4) goals. On RoboTHOR it reaches 33.2 SR, above OWL/CoW 27.5 but below ESC 38.1.
limitations: On RoboTHOR it underperforms ESC (33.2 vs 38.1 SR), and ESC cannot be compared on most PASTURE splits.
Depends on frozen GPT-3.5 with multi-expert prompts, which is costly in queries and latency; no real-robot tests.
Ablations are limited to single splits and evaluation is only in simulation.
